Q: How does Typescript generic auto-inferrence really works on multiple generics? A:

TypeScript either infers all type parameters for a function, or you supply all of them explicitly. There is no middle ground of "infer some, I'll provide others."

b<User>({name: 'string'}) fails because when you write b<User>(...), you are entering explicit type argument mode. TypeScript now expects you to provide every type argument for that function, it won't infer the remaining ones. Since b has two type parameters <T, U>, it demands both:

b<User, Partial<User>>({name: 'string'}) // works, but defeats the purpose

This is by design. The TypeScript team has explicitly decided not to support partial type argument inference in a single call (see microsoft/TypeScript#26349), because the rules for which parameters get inferred vs. provided would be ambiguous and hard to reason about.

As for:

function b<T>() {
    return function<P extends Partial<T>>(p: P) {
        return p
    }
}

b<User>()({name: 'string'})

The current version works because you are now making two separate function calls, each with their own independent inference context:

  1. b<User>() - you explicitly provide T = User for the outer function. This returns a new function whose signature is now concretely <P extends Partial<User>>(p: P) => P.

  2. ({name: 'string'}) - TypeScript infers P fresh for this second call from the argument you pass. No explicit type argument is given, so inference runs freely.

The two calls never compete - each one is either fully explicit or fully inferred on its own.

Q: Create a book manager with a json file using python A:

Understanding the JSON Workflow: Read, Update, and Save

The reason your file is being overwritten is that when you call json.dump(), it starts writing from the beginning of the file, replacing everything that was there. JSON files represent a complete data structure (like a list or a dictionary), so you cannot simply "append" a new object to the end of the file like you would with a plain text log.

The standard workflow for managing data in a JSON file follows these three steps:

  1. Load: Read the existing data from the file into a Python list.

  2. Append: Add your new item to that Python list in memory.

  3. Overwrite: Save the entire updated list back to the file.

Minimal Reproducible Example

Here is a simple way to implement this for your book manager:

import json
import os

FILENAME = 'books.json'

def add_book(new_book_title):
    # 1. Load existing data
    if os.path.exists(FILENAME):
        with open(FILENAME, 'r') as file:
            try:
                books = json.load(file)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                books = [] # Handle empty or corrupted files
    else:
        books = []

    # 2. Append new data
    books.append({"title": new_book_title})

    # 3. Overwrite the file with the updated list
    with open(FILENAME, 'w') as file:
        json.dump(books, file, indent=4)
    
    print(f"Added: {new_book_title}")

# Usage
add_book("The Great Gatsby")
add_book("1984")

Key Concepts for Beginners:

  • json.load() vs json.dump(): Use load to bring data into Python, and dump to send it back to the file.

  • The with statement: Always use with open(...) to ensure the file closes automatically, even if an error occurs.

  • Initialization: Notice the check os.path.exists(). If the file doesn't exist yet, you start with an empty list [].

  • Indentation: The indent=4 argument in json.dump() makes the file human-readable (pretty-print), which is helpful for debugging.

Q: What are the alternatives to SecurityManager for sandboxing untrusted code in Java? A:

https://github.com/pfirmstone/jdk-with-authorization

I have a project on GitHub, that maintains OpenJDK with Authorization, I've taken the SecurityManager, Policy implementation and PolicyWriter (easy to use policy file generator) from JGDMS, and I've added support for Virtual Threads. I've added additional permissions, and removed hard coded static permissions such as URLPermission for applets to contact their originating host, and I've reduced the trusted codebase to the java.base module. Since applet support has been removed, it is easier to prevent the JVM from loading untrusted code through URL injections that would find their way to URLClassLoader in gadget attacks. Furthermore, SecurityManager can no longer be set null by an attacker after being set from the command line.

Note that this shouldn't be used for Sandboxing, it can however be used as part of bytecode auditing and trust establishment, first bytecode should be statically analysed for potential denial of service, then it can be loaded in an isolated JVM running in Hardware Virtual Machine with PolicyWriter enabled and executed. PolicyWriter will generate a POLP policy containing only Permission's required, the generated policy should be reviewed and any unwanted permission grants removed.

Once the code has gained a level of trust using this method, then it can be run with the whitelist generated policy file, if Serialization is used, it will be restricted to only the classes used and listed in the generate policy file, if URL's are accessed, they will be restricted by policy, transitive dependencies will be prevented from loading as will unused Java modules, only authorized dynamic code will be allowed to load, agents will be prevented etc. It's basically a completely locked down fork of OpenJDK's JVM. Note that it has no protections against excessive memory consumption or denial of service type attacks, these need to be cleared with static analysis prior to loading bytecode.

Those wishing to sandbox untrusted Java bytecode should investigate Graal Expresso https://www.graalvm.org/latest/reference-manual/espresso/

Q: Webservice returns 401 when called via ASP.NET Core Blazor Web App A:

First of all, it seems that your JWT Authority is set incorrectly. Currently, you're using: "https://sts.windows.net", which isn't valid for Entra ID v2.

You should change your code to:

jwtOptions.Authority = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/v2.0";

Make sure to replace {tenantId} with your actual TenantId from Entra.
